pr_title: table: drop trailing white spaces in the last cell
pr_comments:
> that's the reason I didn't bother stripping the whitespace in the first place. i.e. figuring out whether some ansi sequence induces a background color or not was something i didn't want to get into

maybe an easy way out is to leave the spaces in when color is enabled, and only suppress it when color is turned off. This would then make thing things look good still on a terminal, but when piped to some pipeline we'll suppres the trailing space, since color is automatically turned off there

issue_context.title: suppress end of line whitespace in table output
issue_context.body:
C.f https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=980820

Please clean up the output of all systemd commands by removing extra
whitespaces at EOL ::

    $ timedatectl status | cat -vTE

                   Local time: Sat 2021-01-30 17:46:26 EET $
               Universal time: Sat 2021-01-30 15:46:26 UTC $
                     RTC time: Sat 2021-01-30 15:46:26     $
                    Time zone: Europe/Helsinki (EET, +0200)$
    System clock synchronized: yes                         $
                  NTP service: active                      $
              RTC in local TZ: no                          $

Debian policy shows ::

    systemd:
      Installed: 247.2-5

NOTE: The output was clean in previous versions ::

    $ timedatectl status | cat -vTE
          Local time: Sat 2021-01-30 17:46:21 EET$
      Universal time: Sat 2021-01-30 15:46:21 UTC$
            RTC time: Sat 2021-01-30 15:46:21$
           Time zone: Europe/Helsinki (EET, +0200)$
     Network time on: yes$
    NTP synchronized: yes$
     RTC in local TZ: no$

Debian policy shows ::

    systemd:
      Installed: 232-8
comments: and how is this a problem?
btw, neither this bug report nor the upstream bug report contains any info why the existing behaviour should be considered a problem?

"Why is this a problem?"

First of all, it's a standard de facto practise that the EOL of the output does not include extra white space. This is how all Linux programs are expected to work by default. 

This behavior was   not present in previous versions of systemd commands

review_comments:
hmm, sounds pointless to first add the space, and then drop it again.  The space should not be added at all in the first place. 

moreover i guess the whitespace should also be suppressed for any alignment
